A1.justification: Both PDFs contain the same AgencyBench study, including the complete 18-page document and Appendix A. Pages 2–18 have identical extracted text and rendered content; the first-page differences are fully inspectable.

before.justification: v1 reports original model evaluations and scaffold comparisons in Tables 1–4, human validation in Sections 3.2–3.3, and tool-use measurements in Appendix Table 6.

after.justification: v3 retains these original empirical results, including model scores, feedback and scaffold comparisons, human validation, and appendix tool-use measurements.

M1.justification: The benchmark construction, agent scaffold, user simulation, Docker sandbox, and rubric-based judging procedures in Section 3 are unchanged. Appendix A.2 retains the same prompts.

E1.justification: Both versions use the same 138 tasks across 32 scenarios and six capabilities, with identical composition in Table 5. The scaffold study retains the same 10-scenario subset.

E2.justification: Table 1 retains the same nine evaluated models. Table 4 retains the same six models and three scaffolds: the authors' scaffold, Claude-Agent-SDK, and OpenAI-Agents-SDK.

E3.justification: The model temperature of 0.7, judge and simulation temperatures of 0.0, 60% passing threshold, feedback limits, validation samples, and scaffold-study protocol are unchanged.

E4.justification: Both versions contain the same human validation, feedback-round comparisons, resource-efficiency analyses, tool-use analyses, and scaffold ablation. The appendix retains the same behavioral discussion and Gomoku scenario example.

E5.justification: Validation sample descriptions and agreement reporting are unchanged, including the 50-task judge validation with kappa 0.93. No run-count, seed, confidence-interval, or significance-testing information is added or revised.

E6.justification: The numerical and qualitative results are unchanged throughout the main text and appendix. Table 1 still reports 56.5 for GPT-5.2 and 38.6 for GLM-4.6. Figure 1's change from 1000k to 1M expresses the same quantity.

T1.justification: The rollout formalization in Section 3.2 and metric definitions in Equations (1)–(3) are unchanged. No mathematical assumptions, derivations, theorems, or proofs are added or revised.

C1.justification: The abstract, introduction, and conclusion retain the same benchmark and automated-evaluation contributions, proprietary versus open-source performance gap, and claims about scaffold-dependent performance.

C2.justification: Interpretations of self-correction, efficiency, tool preferences, and model–scaffold coupling are unchanged. Both retain the limitations concerning incomplete model coverage and restriction to software-based environments on page 10.

D1.justification: v1 already provides the GitHub repository link. v3 adds a first-page resource row with project-site, Hugging Face dataset, and SII Open Source links. This expands documented access; implementation details, settings, and appendix prompts remain unchanged.

R1.justification: Section 2 and all 37 bibliography entries are unchanged. The paper retains the same positioning relative to earlier agent methods and benchmarks.

P1.justification: v3 reorders and renumbers affiliations while preserving author–institution assignments, adds resource-link front matter, and updates the version/date stamp. The main prose, section structure, and appendix wording are unchanged.

P2.justification: v3 adds a resource row with icons and adjusts first-page spacing. Figure 1's comparison table has small formatting changes, including k-to-K capitalization and 1000k-to-1M notation. Pages 2–18 are visually identical.

improvement.justification: v3 adds direct project and dataset pointers beyond v1's repository link, making benchmark resources easier to locate. This provides a limited improvement in access documentation and presentation; the scientific content, evidence, and appendices are unchanged.
